claim: Cassis village centres on a bustling port with cobbled streets, pastel houses and fountain squares; the tourism office recommends strolling flower-filled alleys, harbour terraces and ice cream while watching the boats.
quote: a village that doesn't cheat ... bustling port, cobbled streets, pastel houses and squares with fountains

claim: The Provençal market is held Wednesday and Friday mornings, and Place Baragnon is a notable square in the village.
quote: The Provencal market operates Wednesday and Friday mornings ... Place Baragnon is mentioned as a notable square to visit

claim: The Musée Municipal Méditerranéen d'Arts et Traditions populaires occupies a former 17th-century presbytery near the port, with paintings, Roman artifacts and amphorae, and free admission.
quote: Musée Municipal Méditerranéen d'Arts et Traditions populaires is housed in a former 17th-century presbytery near the port, featuring paintings, Roman artifacts, amphorae ... free admission

claim: The Château de Cassis grew from a 5th-century Roman watch tower, was occupied by the powerful Baux family from 1223, and François des Baux built bulwarks around its four square 8-metre towers and added a Saint-Michel church between 1372-1380.
quote: François des Baux strengthened maritime defenses by building bulwarks around the four square 8-metre high towers. Between 1372–1380, he added a well, baker's oven, and a church dedicated to Saint-Michel.

claim: The castle was largely destroyed by Charles V's imperial forces in 1524, inspected by General Bonaparte on 10 February 1794, bought by a tobacco grower in 1896, and today operates as exclusive guest accommodation with eight luxury suites.
quote: destruction in 1524 when imperial forces attacked under Charles V's command. General Bonaparte famously inspected the artillery there on February 10, 1794 ... Today it operates as an exclusive guest accommodation featuring eight luxury suites.

claim: The Provençal motto attributed to Frédéric Mistral is 'Qu'a vist Paris, se noun a vist Cassis, n'a rèn vist' — 'Who has seen Paris and not Cassis, has not seen anything.'
quote: Qu'a vist Paris, se noun a vist Cassis, n'a rèn vist ... Who has seen Paris and not Cassis, has not seen anything.

claim: Cassis's port is a near-perfect crescent of ochre and pastel facades where café terraces fill by late morning and shaded squares host unhurried games of pétanque.
quote: a near-perfect crescent lined with faded ochre and pastel façades ... Shaded squares become informal gathering places where games of pétanque play out at an unhurried pace.

claim: The Église Saint-Michel in Cassis is a heritage church in the historic centre worth visiting.
quote: Saint Michael's Church (Cassis) | Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism

claim: The port of Cassis is the centre of daily life, with colourful fishing boats and yachts side by side, fishermen selling their catch by day and dining terraces with sea views by evening.
quote: the port is where a lot of life and history took place ... colourful fishing boats and yachts lie side by side, and fishermen sell their catch during the day while evening terraces fill with people dining with a view of the sea
